rules.title: Prohibition on coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents (BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell or provide, coordinated pricing algorithms that use nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. The City Attorney or an aggrieved tenant can sue for damages, injunctive relief and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, with attorney's fees to the prevailing party.
rules.key_value: ban on coordinated pricing algorithms using nonpublic competitor data (<90 days old); up to $1,000 per violation
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley
rules.effective_date_note: Ordinance text (D001) states no effective date (passed to print Nov 18, 2025). January 2026 taken from the Aug 2026 law-firm alert.
rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated anonymous reports, affordable-housing rent/income limit tools, market research for financing, appraisals, and software research/testing/training.
rules.penalty: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (each month and each unit separate); damages, injunctive relief, restitution, attorney's fees
rules.conflict_note: Two published effective dates: January 2026 (law-firm alert) vs March 1, 2026 (reported as ordinance text, not stated in the provided ordinance document).

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decisions to rent or end a tenancy. If a landlord takes action based on criminal history, they must give written notice and a chance to respond.
rules.key_value: ban on criminal-history inquiries and use in tenant selection; fines $1,000-$10,000 per violation
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making
rules.effective_date_note: Only the Council passage date (April 14, 2020) is stated.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited public housing/Section 8 exemptions; owner-occupied 1-3 unit properties; owner move-back units; existing tenants subletting or adding roommates.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines $1,000-$10,000 per violation, damages (actual or 3x monthly rent), punitive damages, fees, injunctive relief.

unverifiable_exemptions: units under owner move-back rental agreement
existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause (Just Cause) for Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords of fully or partially covered units may evict only for just cause. Measure BB bars eviction for rental debt under one month of HUD Fair Market Rent or for refusing to sign a new fixed-term lease; lease-breach evictions need a specific notice and substantial actual harm; termination notices must direct tenants to the Rent Board and be filed with it within 3 business days.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; no eviction for rent debt under 1 month FMR
rules.quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”)
rules.effective_date_note: Measure BB passed by voters Nov 2024; the just-cause requirement itself predates it. No explicit effective date stated for the eviction provisions.
rules.exemptions: Golden duplex, owner-shared kitchen/bath, owner-occupied ADU properties (tenancies after Nov 7, 2018), university dorms, nonprofit cooperatives.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner shares kitchen or bath with tenant

rules.title: Owner move-in and Ellis Act eviction relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Owners must pay tenants relocation assistance when evicting for an owner move-in or to withdraw the unit from the rental market. From Jan 1, 2026 the standard payment is $19,413, plus $6,471 more for qualifying households, adjusted yearly with CPI.
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction
rules.effective_date_note: Date the 2026 inflation-adjusted amounts took effect (Rent Board approved Oct 16, 2025); the underlying requirement predates this.

unverifiable_exemptions: exemptions under the Rent Ordinance not stated in this document

rules.review_note: Code section for relocation not stated in D004; ch. 13.76 inferred from the Rent Ordinance name.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance - Annual General Adjustment (max 5%)
rules.requirement: For fully covered units (mostly multifamily built before 1980, plus older single-family tenancies), the yearly rent increase follows a CPI-based formula (65% of CPI) and can never exceed 5%. The 2026 AGA is 1.0%. Newer construction, most condos and later single-family tenancies have no rent ceiling.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%
rules.effective_date_note: Measure BB (Nov 2024) added the 5% cap; page gives no explicit date, approximated. 2026 AGA effective no earlier than 2026-01-01.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered units: most multifamily units built before 1980, single-family homes with tenancies before 1996, rooming houses.
rules.exemptions: Partially covered units (CO after June 1980, post-1996 single-family tenancies, most condos) and some federally restricted subsidized units have no rent ceiling.
rules.interaction: Local rent control governs; units under it are generally exempt from the state Tenant Protection Act cap.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family tenancies before 1996 are covered regardless of build date; condos mostly partially covered
certain Section 202/811 and HUD-insured subsidized units

rules.review_note: Cutoff approximated from 'built before 1980' / 'CO after June 1980'; exact day not stated.

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: For units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on the security deposit at the end of each year, and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before year end.
rules.key_value: annual interest on deposit, prorated at move-out
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year
rules.exemptions: Exempt units: golden duplex, owner-shared kitchen/bath, owner-occupied ADU property, university dorms, nonprofit cooperatives.
rules.review_note: Code section not stated in documents; ch. 13.76 inferred from Rent Ordinance name.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening and application fee rules (BMC ch. 13.78)
rules.requirement: Owners charging a screening fee must give a Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and state the maximum state fee cap before receiving the fee. Owners cannot charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or to add or replace a roommate.
rules.key_value: Disclosure of fee rights and state cap ($68.96 for 2026); no non-refundable renewal fees
rules.quoted_span: the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
rules.effective_date_note: Effective date not stated in documents.
